pages.title: Project Overview
pages.purpose: High-level introduction to Feishu-LongTerm-Mem: what it does, why it exists, key architectural concepts, and how the major subsystems fit together. Links to child pages for deeper coverage.

pages.title: Getting Started & Configuration
pages.purpose: Setup instructions, environment variables (.env), dependency management (pyproject.toml / uv.lock), MCP client configuration (mcp-claude-config.json), and how to run the system for the first time.

pages.title: System Architecture & Data Flow
pages.purpose: End-to-end data flow from Feishu IM/Docs ingestion through detection, episode management, LLM extraction, memory graph storage, and MCP exposure. Describes the detector-engine-storage pattern and key design decisions.

pages.title: Ingestion & Detection Layer
pages.purpose: Overview of how raw Feishu messages and documents are ingested, filtered, and classified as decision signals. Links to child pages covering IM detection, document detection, and episode management.

pages.title: Feishu IM Detector
pages.purpose: Details the LarkIMDetector and its two modes (polling and WebSocket), the EnhancedDetector heuristic scoring pipeline (LexicalAnalyzer, StructuralAnalyzer, DynamicAnalyzer, PatternMatcherV2), anti-signal filtering, and burst-mode polling logic.

pages.title: Document Detector & Debounce Tracker
pages.purpose: Covers DocAdapter (local filesystem polling, SHA-256 hashing, planned Lark API integration), DocDebounceTracker (state persistence, debounce window logic), DocDetector (signal scoring, job creation), and the doc_detector module.

pages.title: Episode Management
pages.purpose: Explains how individual messages are buffered into Episodes by EpisodeManager, the time-gap and semantic-threshold boundary detection, the run_episode_check_loop reaper, and how episodes are dispatched to the MemoryEngine.

pages.title: LLM & Extraction Layer
pages.purpose: Overview of how raw text (episodes, documents) is transformed into structured DecisionNode objects via LLM calls. Links to child pages for the LLM client, extractors, and prompt library.

pages.title: LLM Client & Error Handling
pages.purpose: Documents the LLMClient (OpenAI-compatible wrapper), LLMConfig, TokenTracker, and the error_handling subsystem (circuit breaker, guardrails, retry/recovery logic).

pages.title: Decision Extractors
pages.purpose: Covers SimpleLLMExtractor (IM/episode extraction), DocDecisionExtractor (document extraction, deduplication, conflict assessment, update detection), and the conv_episode_extractor and fact_extractors modules.

pages.title: Prompt Library
pages.purpose: Catalogs all prompt modules (decision_prompts, doc_decision_prompts, conv_prompts, episode_prompts, fact_prompts, topic_prompts, answer_prompts) and explains how prompts are structured and used by extractors.

pages.title: Memory Graph & Storage
pages.purpose: Overview of the dual-layer persistence architecture: in-memory MemoryGraph for fast querying and Git-backed GitStorage for versioned persistence. Links to child pages for each layer.

pages.title: MemoryGraph (In-Memory Index)
pages.purpose: Deep dive into MemoryGraph: five internal indices, DecisionNode schema, hot score algorithm, conflict detection via CONFLICTS_WITH relations, dirty-node tracking, and the GitReader protocol.

pages.title: Git Storage Backend
pages.purpose: Explains GitStorage CRUD operations, the decision branch-per-record strategy, file format (YAML frontmatter + Markdown body), commit message conventions, GitCLI wrapper, git_format serialization, and auto-push configuration.

pages.title: Hypergraph Structure & Retrieval
pages.purpose: Covers the three-layer hypergraph (FactNode/L1, EpisodeNode/L2, TopicNode/L3), HypergraphBuilder, HierarchicalRetriever (BM25 + vector fusion), and the graph/builder and graph/retrieval modules.

pages.title: Core Engine & Pipeline
pages.purpose: Overview of the MemoryEngine orchestrator and PipelineEngine mutation processor. Links to child pages for the engine lifecycle and the DecisionNode/mutation data model.

pages.title: MemoryEngine Lifecycle
pages.purpose: Details MemoryEngine initialization, the detector loop, sync loop (dirty-node flushing), semantic reconnection of episodes, deduplication via embedding+reranker+LLM judge, conflict detection, and graceful shutdown.

pages.title: DecisionNode & Mutation Model
pages.purpose: Documents the DecisionNode Pydantic schema (all fields, roles, status state machine), DecisionMutation command types (CREATE, UPDATE, STATUS_CHANGE, CONFLICT_MERGE, OBJECTION, REVERT, DEPRECATE), and PipelineEngine.apply_mutation dispatch logic.

pages.title: Semantic Search (Embedding & Reranking)
pages.purpose: Overview of the two-stage semantic retrieval pipeline: EmbeddingProvider for vector search and RerankerProvider for relevance scoring. Links to child pages for each provider.

pages.title: EmbeddingProvider
pages.purpose: Covers EmbeddingProvider initialization, the embed() batch API, cosine_similarity utility, connection pooling with HTTPAdapter, exponential backoff retry strategy, and Qwen3-Embedding model validation.

pages.title: RerankerProvider
pages.purpose: Covers RerankerProvider dual-path execution (REST /v1/rerank vs vLLM /v1/completions logprobs), the yes/no softmax scoring formula, single vs. batch query routing, and fallback behavior.

pages.title: MCP Server
pages.purpose: Overview of the Model Context Protocol server that exposes the decision memory system to AI clients (Claude Desktop, OpenClaw). Links to child pages for tool categories and server configuration.

pages.title: MCP Tool Reference
pages.purpose: Comprehensive reference for all 34 MCP tools grouped by category: Query tools (list_decisions, search, topic, timeline, stats, hot_decisions, forgotten_decisions), Writing tools (create_decision, update_decision, confirm_decision, reject_decision, revert_decision, resolve_conflict), LLM-assisted tools (extract_decision, check_conflict, evaluate_dedup), and Git/system tools (git_history, git_blame, refresh).

pages.title: MCP Server Deployment
pages.purpose: Explains how to launch the MCP server via `uv run`, configure it in Claude Desktop or OpenClaw (mcp-claude-config.json), required environment variables (MODEL_NAME, BASE_URL, API_KEY, STORAGE_PATH), and the stdio transport protocol.

pages.title: Notification & Push System
pages.purpose: Overview of the PushEngine that delivers decision cards to Feishu/Lark, terminal, and macOS notifications. Links to child pages for the card renderer and push scheduling.

pages.title: PushEngine & Scheduling
pages.purpose: Details PushEngine triggers (CONFLICT, DECISION_UPDATE, HOT_SCORE_LOW, SCHEDULED_DAILY, SCHEDULED_WEEKLY, MANUAL_QUERY), the hot score decay/increment system, daily/weekly summary loops, multi-channel dispatch (Feishu interactive card, terminal, osascript), and error degradation.

pages.title: Card Renderer
pages.purpose: Covers CardRenderer output formats (Feishu interactive card JSON, Markdown), decision card layout, conflict card comparative view, and daily summary format.

pages.title: Evaluation Framework
pages.purpose: Overview of the extraction evaluation system used to benchmark LLM decision-extraction accuracy. Links to child pages for the evaluator and the eval dataset.

pages.title: Evaluator & Scenarios
pages.purpose: Documents the ExtractionEvaluator (run_extraction_eval), the 12 evaluation scenarios (technical-selection through boundary-case), evaluation dimensions (detection, content, proposer, executor, impact_level, status), the QA multiple-choice format, and the eval report schema.

pages.title: Eval Dataset
pages.purpose: Describes the eval_data/decision_extraction/ directory structure (dialogue.json + qa.json per scenario), the 12 scenario types and their Chinese-language dialogue examples, and how to add new scenarios.
